+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+"""K1's qkv GEMV (DESIGN_BC 5.5, Phase B1) on the GEMV CTAs b in [NA, BLOCKS),
+g = b - NA: this rank's 2304 qkv rows (``qkv_proj``, column-parallel: q 1024
+| k 128 | v 128 | og 1024) against the boundary's ``attn_in`` rows.
+
+Stock reference: ``wvSplitK`` (S <= 5) / hipBLASLt (S = 8) / ``F.linear``:
+an fp32 dot over K = 8192, rounded to bf16 once. Here the K1 stage hands
+fp32 partial rows to the epilogue, which adds the two contributors and
+rounds once (``front/epilogue.py``)::
+
+    tasks    tau = 16 T + kp: tile T (16 rows 16 T ..) x K part kp (512
+             columns, 4 chunks of 128); CTA g runs tau = 12 g + i, i < 12,
+             12 distinct K parts (consecutive mod 16, no wrap inside a tile)
+    rounds   r = 0 .. 5: waves 0-3 task 2 r, waves 4-7 task 2 r + 1; wave w
+             chunk w % 4 of its task (``gemv.loads``: 4 dwordx4 a lane,
+             nontemporal); rounds 0 .. EARLY - 1 issued at entry, the rest
+             right after the ``arow`` loads
+    B rows   ``arow`` (bf16 [MT, 8192], the boundary's, device scope) of the
+             CTA's 12 K parts, S rows each, staged into LDS ``xa`` in one
+             batched pass (every load, the late weight rounds, then every
+             ds_write, one barrier) behind the ``ardy`` flags of the 48
+             slices they cover
+    sums     a task's value: its 4 waves' accumulators in wave order
+             (``row_sum``); a tile's partial in this CTA: its tasks in K part
+             order -> ``qpart`` ((T 2 + c) MT + t) 16 + r, contributor c = g
+             - ``contributors(T)[0]`` (0: the lower K parts)
+
+Every tile has exactly ``K1_MAXC`` = 2 contributors (``spec.k1_contributor0``),
+each puts its partial of every row of every token, zeros
+included, so the epilogue's waits depend on nothing but the GEMV CTAs. The
+order (waves, then K parts, then contributors) is fixed and the same on
+every rank: ``qkvo`` and the cache are rank-bit-identical.
+
+Rule 8 (DESIGN_BC 10.4): a GEMV CTA polls ``ardy`` holding only its own
+weights in flight; it publishes nothing. ``vmcnt`` retires in order, so the
+poll's ``vmcnt(0)`` (``_spin``) and the staging pass's ds_writes wait for
+every weight load issued before them: only the EARLY rounds (128 of the
+CTA's 192 KiB) are, the last rounds stream behind the ``arow`` loads, so the
+ds_writes wait on a counted ``vmcnt`` (the late rounds' loads still in
+flight) and the poll and staging round trips hide under the stream's tail.
+
+``stages/gemv.py`` is K2's (compiled into every K2 build) and is not edited:
+the staging pass and the task sums are here.
+"""
+
+import functools
+
+import flydsl.expr as fx
+from flydsl.expr import gpu, range_constexpr, rocdl
+
+from vllm.models.muse_spark.amd.specialized_decode.mono.common.ops import (
+    ld_dev,
+    mfma_bf16,
+    row_sum,
+    traced,
+)
+from vllm.models.muse_spark.amd.specialized_decode.mono.common.plan import (
+    THREADS,
+    cdiv,
+)
+from vllm.models.muse_spark.amd.specialized_decode.mono.spec import (
+    AROW,
+    COLS,
+    HIDDEN,
+    K1_MAXC,
+    K1_ROUNDS,
+    K1_TPC,
+    KPART,
+    KPARTS,
+    ROWS,
+    WAVES,
+    ardy_pair,
+    k1_contributor0,
+    qpart_pair,
+)
+from vllm.models.muse_spark.amd.specialized_decode.mono.stages import gemv
+
+STAGE = "qkv"
+XA_ROW = KPART + gemv.LDS_PAD  # bf16 a padded LDS K part row (520)
+X4 = KPART // 8  # dwordx4 a K part row (64)
+CHUNKS = KPART // gemv.KCH  # 4 chunks a K part: one a wave of a half
+SLICES = KPART // COLS  # boundary slices (``ardy`` flags) a K part covers
+EARLY = 4  # weight rounds issued at entry; the rest after the arow loads
+assert CHUNKS * 2 == WAVES and K1_ROUNDS * 2 == K1_TPC
+assert SLICES * K1_TPC <= THREADS  # a flag a polling thread
+assert 0 < EARLY < K1_ROUNDS
+
+
+def tau_of(g, i):
+    """Task i of GEMV CTA g."""
+    return K1_TPC * g + i
+
+
+@functools.cache
+def lds_struct(s: int):
+    """The stage's LDS: the CTA's 12 K parts of rows 0 .. s-1 of ``arow``,
+    task i's row t at ``(i s + t) XA_ROW`` bf16 (99,840 B at s = 8). Cached:
+    one struct type a width."""
+
+    @fx.struct
+    class QkvLds:
+        xa: fx.Array[fx.Int32, K1_TPC * s * XA_ROW // 2, 16]
+
+    return QkvLds
+
+
+def contributors(tile):
+    """(the first GEMV CTA g whose tasks cover ``tile``, the contributors a
+    tile has): the tile's K parts are split between g (the lower ones) and
+    g + 1. Python ints (host) or traced Int32 (in-kernel) alike."""
+    return k1_contributor0(tile), K1_MAXC
+
+
+def task(g, i):
+    """GEMV CTA g's task i: (tile T, K part kp)."""
+    tau = tau_of(g, i)
+    return tau // KPARTS, tau % KPARTS
+
+
+def last_of_tile(g, i):
+    """Whether task i is the last of its tile in CTA g (its partial is
+    complete): i == K1_TPC - 1, or task i + 1 starts the next tile. True (a
+    Python bool) for i == K1_TPC - 1, else a traced Boolean (Python bool for
+    an int g)."""
+    if i == K1_TPC - 1:
+        return True
+    return (tau_of(g, i) + 1) % KPARTS == 0
+
+
+def qkv_loads(c, g, rounds) -> list:
+    """GEMV CTA g's weights of ``rounds``: round r's task 2 r + h (h = wave
+    // 4), chunk wave % 4 of its K part, 4 dwordx4 a lane (nontemporal),
+    every round in flight (6: 96 VGPRs). The EARLY rounds are the CTA's first
+    loads, the rest are issued by ``stage_rows``. A scheduling barrier after
+    them keeps every load where it is issued (LLVM would sink the late rounds
+    to their MFMAs)."""
+    lane, wave = c["lane"], c["wave"]
+    w4 = wave % CHUNKS
+    half = wave // CHUNKS
+    w = c["args"]["w_qkv"]
+    ops = []
+    for r in rounds:
+        tile, kp = task(g, 2 * r + half)
+        ops.append(
+            gemv.loads(lane, w4, w, tile * ROWS, KPART, ldk=HIDDEN, k0=kp * KPART)[0]
+        )
+    rocdl.sched_barrier(0)
+    return ops
+
+
+def _stage_ij(v, s):
+    """A staging element v -> (task i, token t, dwordx4 x of the K part)."""
+    return v // (s * X4), v // X4 % s, v % X4
+
+
+def stage_rows(c, g) -> list:
+    """The one staging pass: the ``arow`` rows (device scope: the boundary
+    CTAs of this launch wrote them) of the CTA's 12 K parts -> LDS ``xa``, 16
+    B a thread a round (12 S 64 dwordx4: 12 rounds at S = 8), every round's
+    load issued before the first ds_write, then one barrier. The K parts are
+    (12 g + i) % 16, derived from g in-kernel. Between the loads and the
+    ds_writes it issues the late weight rounds (EARLY ..) and returns them:
+    younger than the ``arow`` loads, they stay in flight through the
+    ds_writes and the barrier.
+
+    Not ``ops.batched_rounds``: its last round's store is predicated (v <
+    n), so LLVM sinks that round's load into the branch, behind the earlier
+    rounds' stores (two round trips at S = 1). Here a round past the end
+    loads and stores element n - 1 again (the same bytes to the same LDS
+    word), so nothing is predicated and every load stays ahead."""
+    s, tid = c["S"], c["tid"]
+    arow = c["scr"][AROW]
+    xa = c["lds"][STAGE]["xa"]
+    total = K1_TPC * s * X4
+    vs = [fx.min(tid + THREADS * i, total - 1) for i in range(cdiv(total, THREADS))]
+    got = []
+    for v in vs:
+        i, t, x = _stage_ij(v, s)
+        kp = tau_of(g, i) % KPARTS
+        word = (t * HIDDEN + kp * KPART + 8 * x) // 2
+        got.append(fx.Vector(ld_dev(arow, word, 4)))
+    rocdl.sched_barrier(0)
+    late = qkv_loads(c, g, range(EARLY, K1_ROUNDS))
+    for v, w in zip(vs, got):
+        i, t, x = _stage_ij(v, s)
+        fx.ptr_store(w, xa + ((i * s + t) * XA_ROW + 8 * x) // 2)
+    gpu.barrier()
+    return late
+
+
+@traced
+def _poll_ardy(c, g):
+    """Thread i < 48: the ``ardy`` flag of slice 4 kp + i % 4
+    of the CTA's task i // 4's K part kp; then a barrier."""
+    tid = c["tid"]
+    if tid < SLICES * K1_TPC:
+        kp = tau_of(g, tid // SLICES) % KPARTS
+        c["poll"]([(c["scr"]["ardy"], ardy_pair(SLICES * kp + tid % SLICES), 1)])
+    gpu.barrier()
+
+
+def _mfmas(c, r, ops):
+    """Round r: this wave's 16x16 accumulator of its task's chunk (4 MFMAs of
+    32 K against the staged rows of tokens 0 .. S-1)."""
+    s, lane, wave = c["S"], c["lane"], c["wave"]
+    xa = c["lds"][STAGE]["xa"]
+    w4 = wave % CHUNKS
+    half = wave // CHUNKS
+    t = fx.min(lane % ROWS, s - 1)
+    row = (2 * r + half) * s + t
+    kk = w4 * gemv.KCH + lane // ROWS * 8
+    acc = fx.Vector.filled(4, 0.0, fx.Float32)
+    for q in range_constexpr(4):
+        xb = fx.Vector(
+            fx.ptr_load(
+                xa + (row * XA_ROW + kk + 32 * q) // 2,
+                result_type=fx.Vector.make_type(4, fx.Int32),
+            )
+        )
+        acc = mfma_bf16(ops[q].bitcast(fx.BFloat16), xb.bitcast(fx.BFloat16), acc)
+    return acc
+
+
+@traced
+def stage_qkv(c, g, ops) -> None:
+    """GEMV CTA g: the ``ardy`` polls (its EARLY weight rounds ``ops`` in
+    flight) -> the staging pass (which issues the late rounds) -> the rounds
+    of MFMAs; thread (t, r) = (tid // 16, tid % 16), t < S, adds each task's
+    row r of token t to the tile's partial and puts it to ``qpart`` when the
+    CTA's last task of the tile is in.
+    Ends with a barrier (``red`` and ``xa`` handed over)."""
+    s, tid, lane, wave, red = c["S"], c["tid"], c["lane"], c["wave"], c["red"]
+    qpart = c["scr"]["qpart"]
+    _poll_ardy(c, g)
+    ops = ops + stage_rows(c, g)
+    r16 = tid % ROWS
+    t = tid // ROWS
+    tc = fx.min(t, s - 1)  # threads past S read token S - 1's (in bounds)
+    live = t < s
+    zero = fx.Float32(0.0)
+    part = zero
+    for r in range_constexpr(K1_ROUNDS):
+        acc = _mfmas(c, r, ops[r])
+        fx.ptr_store(acc, red + (wave * 64 + lane) * 4)
+        gpu.barrier()
+        for h in range_constexpr(2):
+            i = 2 * r + h
+            part = part + row_sum(red, r16, tc, range(CHUNKS * h, CHUNKS * (h + 1)))
+            tile, _ = task(g, i)
+            last = last_of_tile(g, i)
+            put = live if last is True else live & last
+            if put:
+                pair = qpart_pair(tile, g - contributors(tile)[0], t, r16)
+                c["put"](qpart, pair, part)
+            part = zero if last is True else fx.Float32(last.select(zero, part))
+        gpu.barrier()

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+"""K1: one Muse Spark kernel layer's attention front (Phase B1, DESIGN_BC 5),
+from the previous layer's deferred FFN boundary to the qkv rows and this
+step's K / V in the cache, in one launch a layer and rank. It replaces vLLM's
+``_norm_residual_norm`` boundary, the qkv GEMM and the fused QK-norm / RoPE /
+KV insert; the stock attention core and K2 follow it.
+
+    boundary      CTAs 0 .. 63, no weight: the previous layer's post_ffn_norm
+                  (weight first), the gated blend and this layer's
+                  pre_qkv_proj_norm on slice j (``front/boundary.py``) ->
+                  ``stream_out``, the ``arow`` rows, ``ardy[j]``
+    epilogue      CTAs 0 .. 5 S - 1, after their slice: unit u = (token u // 5,
+                  row group u % 5) (``front/epilogue.py``): the two GEMV
+                  partials -> QK-norm, RoPE (``rope`` builds) -> ``qkvo``, the
+                  k / v heads into the cache
+    qkv           CTAs 64 .. 255: 12 (tile, K part) tasks each, the first
+                  weight rounds in flight from entry, the ``arow`` rows
+                  staged behind ``ardy``, the last rounds behind the rows'
+                  loads (``front/qkv.py``) -> ``qpart``
+
+The roles are split by CTA (5.3) so that no CTA polls or publishes with a
+load in flight that is not its own task's (rule 8, DESIGN_BC 10.4): the
+boundary CTAs issue no weight load (their polls hold the boundary operands
+and the epilogue's three step inputs), the epilogue polls ``qpart`` holding
+only its cos / sin row, a GEMV CTA polls ``ardy`` holding only its own
+weights. The boundary CTAs wait only on each other, the GEMV CTAs only on the
+boundary, the epilogue only on the GEMV CTAs; every CTA is resident (one a
+CU, below), so the launch cannot deadlock. A wait that gives up records
+itself and fails the rank (``sync._spin``); every address stays clamped and
+a FAILED rank writes no K / V, so the launch completes.
+
+K1 is rank-local (E2): the qkv rows are this rank's column shard and the
+boundary's inputs are replicated, so it takes no ``peers`` and pushes nothing
+to another rank (only ``alarm``, on a give-up). Its tags carry the layer's K1
+slot (``spec.k1_slot``), so a step's K1 and K2 pairs never alias. The step
+epoch is the one K2 reads: the step's first kernel layer bumps it before its
+K1 (``runtime.layers``).
+
+LDS: the fixed ``red`` (the GEMV's accumulators), no ``RouteLds``, then a
+union of the GEMV's staged rows (``qkv``) and the residency pin (``pin``).
+The pin makes every build hold more than half a CU's LDS, so the dispatcher
+places one CTA a CU (5.9): at S <= 2 the code alone (~120 VGPRs, 20 KiB)
+would let two CTAs share a CU and leave CUs without a GEMV CTA. The
+``amdgpu-waves-per-eu`` attribute 5.9 names is a register-allocation bound,
+not an occupancy one (the hardware places by the descriptor's VGPR granules
+and LDS), so it cannot do this. The epilogue and the boundary use no LDS.
+
+Adapted from K2 (``mono/layer.py``: the kernel / launcher pair, ``build``,
+``k2_launch``), with the context built rank-local
+(``make_context(peers=False, route_lds=False)``) and the arguments packed by
+name.
+"""
+
+from collections.abc import Mapping
+
+import flydsl.compiler as flyc
+import flydsl.expr as fx
+import torch
+from flydsl.expr.typing import Int32, Int64
+
+from vllm.models.muse_spark.amd.specialized_decode.mono import spec
+from vllm.models.muse_spark.amd.specialized_decode.mono.common.context import (
+    RED_WORDS,
+    lds_total_bytes,
+    make_context,
+    settle,
+)
+from vllm.models.muse_spark.amd.specialized_decode.mono.common.ops import traced
+from vllm.models.muse_spark.amd.specialized_decode.mono.common.plan import (
+    LDS_BYTES,
+    THREADS,
+    KernelAbi,
+    key_tuple,
+    source_digest,
+)
+from vllm.models.muse_spark.amd.specialized_decode.mono.front import (
+    boundary,
+    epilogue,
+    qkv,
+)
+from vllm.models.muse_spark.amd.specialized_decode.mono.layer import _bind_cache
+from vllm.models.muse_spark.amd.specialized_decode.mono.spec import (
+    BLOCKS,
+    E_UNITS,
+    K1_GEMV0,
+    NA,
+    K1Build,
+)
+
+# The kernel's parameters: spec.K1_ARGS, the residual stream renamed
+# ``stream_in`` as in K2 (the launcher's own ``stream`` is the HIP stream);
+# ``k1_launch`` and ``c["args"]`` key them by K1_ARGS.
+KERNEL_NAMES = {"stream": "stream_in"}
+ABI = KernelAbi(tuple(KERNEL_NAMES.get(n, n) for n in spec.K1_ARGS))
+# Every .py under mono/: joins every build key (K2's digest; the front stages
+# and the helpers K1 shares with K2 are all in it)
+SOURCES = source_digest(".")
+REGIONS = spec.REGIONS  # debug.region_ids order of the wait records
+# ``program``'s two role branches partition the grid: every CTA runs exactly
+# one of them
+assert K1_GEMV0 == NA and E_UNITS * spec.MAX_ROWS <= NA
+
+# One CTA a CU (DESIGN_BC 5.9): every build's LDS past half a CU's
+RESIDENT_LDS = LDS_BYTES // 2 + 16
+PIN_WORDS = (RESIDENT_LDS - RED_WORDS * 4) // 4
+
+
+@fx.struct
+class PinLds:
+    pin: fx.Array[fx.Int32, PIN_WORDS, 16]
+
+
+_STREAM = fx.Stream(None)
+
+
+def lds_structs(s: int) -> dict:
+    """The stage union's members at ``s`` rows: the GEMV's staged ``arow``
+    rows and the residency pin (no stage touches it)."""
+    return {qkv.STAGE: qkv.lds_struct(s), "pin": PinLds}
+
+
+def lds_bytes(s: int) -> int:
+    """K1's static LDS at ``s`` rows: ``red``, then the union (no
+    ``RouteLds``). Past ``LDS_BYTES // 2`` at every width."""
+    return lds_total_bytes(lds_structs(s), route_lds=False)
+
+
+@traced
+def program(c) -> None:
+    """K1's roles on CTA ``c["bid"]`` (DESIGN_BC 5.3). Every branch is
+    CTA-uniform, so every thread reaches every barrier."""
+    s = c["S"]
+    b = c["bid"]
+    b32 = fx.Int32(b)
+    # -- the weight-free CTAs: every operand of the boundary and the
+    # epilogue's step inputs issued before the boundary's first poll; the
+    # epilogue after the slice's publish
+    if b < NA:
+        pre = boundary.boundary_loads(c, b)
+        epi = boundary.epilogue_inputs(c, b)
+        settle(c)
+        boundary.stage_boundary(c, b, pre)
+        if b32 < E_UNITS * s:
+            epilogue.stage_epilogue(c, b32, epi)
+    # -- the GEMV CTAs: their early weight rounds the first loads, then the
+    # ardy polls (the late rounds go out behind the arow loads)
+    if b >= K1_GEMV0:
+        g = b32 - K1_GEMV0
+        wops = qkv.qkv_loads(c, g, range(qkv.EARLY))
+        settle(c)
+        qkv.stage_qkv(c, g, wops)
+
+
+_BUILDS: dict = {}
+
+
+def build(key: K1Build):
+    """The ``@flyc.jit`` launcher of build ``key`` (``ABI`` order, then
+    ``stream``), cached. Every field of ``key`` and the mono sources are in
+    the JIT key (``key_tuple``), referenced by both the kernel and the
+    launcher."""
+    if key in _BUILDS:
+        return _BUILDS[key]
+    if not isinstance(key, K1Build):
+        raise TypeError(f"a K1 build key is a K1Build, not {type(key).__name__}")
+    s = key.tokens
+    lds = lds_structs(s)
+    nbytes = lds_bytes(s)
+    if nbytes > LDS_BYTES:
+        raise ValueError(f"K1 at {s} rows: {nbytes} B of LDS > {LDS_BYTES}")
+    keyed = key_tuple(key, SOURCES)
+
+    @flyc.kernel(name=key.kernel_name(), known_block_size=[THREADS, 1, 1])
+    def k1(
+        branch: Int64,
+        stream_in: Int64,
+        pad: Int64,
+        positions: Int64,
+        slots: Int64,
+        w_postffn: Int64,
+        ffn_alpha: Int64,
+        ffn_beta: Int64,
+        w_preqkv: Int64,
+        w_qkv: Int64,
+        cos_sin: Int64,
+        kv: Int64,
+        kv_sb: Int64,
+        kv_sh: Int64,
+        kv_st: Int64,
+        kv_blocks: Int32,
+        max_pos: Int32,
+        stream_out: Int64,
+        qkvo: Int64,
+        scratch: Int64,
+        rank: Int32,

+"""K2: one Muse Spark decoder layer from the attention's gated core (o_proj's
+input) to the layer's deferred FFN boundary, in one launch a layer and rank.
+
+    o_proj        every CTA: tasks b and b + 256 (16 rows each), the partials
+                  pushed to every rank (``ar``)
+    seam          CTAs 0 .. 63: the AR reduce (rank order, fp32) and the
+                  attention boundary (post_attn_norm, gated blend, pre_ffn_norm)
+                  -> ``stream_out``, the ffn_in rows (``xrow``), XRDY
+    route         CTAs 0 .. S-1, after their seam slice: row t's top-8
+    router        CTAs 64 .. 95: one fp32 router row each -> every rank's logits
+    pooler        CTAs 96 .. 223: 32 row groups x 4 K quarters -> every rank's
+                  pooled rows
+    xq            every CTA that can get a ug task (b >= spec.ug_cta0(S): 128
+                  at S = 1, else every CTA): the pooled rows -> pre-expert
+                  norm -> MXFP4 (LDS)
+    union, ug     every CTA: the step's union of experts; gate/up tasks reversed
+                  over the grid (CTA b: 255 - b, + 256, ...)
+    down          every CTA b: pooled rows 16 b .. of every union expert ->
+                  the column owner's ``rsx`` (always, zeros included)
+    owner         CTAs 32 rank .. + 32: the rank-order reduce, the post-expert
+                  norm (sum of squares exchanged), route weights, top-k sum
+                  -> every rank's ``moe``
+    unpool        every CTA: its row group's K quarter -> every rank's branch
+    gather        CTAs 0 .. 63: the branch rows -> ``branch_out``
+
+The attention core K2 starts from is the build's ``K2Build.core`` (one kernel
+template, a variant a core; ``ABI_BY_CORE``): "tensor" (Phase A) reads
+vLLM's gated core ``core``; "gated" (Phase B2, DESIGN_BC 6) reads vLLM's
+attention output ``attn`` and the qkv rows ``qkvo`` and computes the output
+norm and gate in its core load (``attention/gate.py``), those loads issued
+before the o_proj weights; "split" (Phase C, the q = 1 widths, DESIGN_BC 7)
+reads the qkv rows ``qkvo``, the layer's KV cache and its KV group's block
+table and sequence lengths and runs the attention core itself:
+
+    split         CTAs 0 .. n_units - 1: one split-KV unit each
+                  (``attention/split.py``) -> partials, ``srdy``
+    combine       CTAs C0 = 256 - 16 S ..: one (token, q head) each
+                  (``attention/combine.py``): the units' partials merged, the
+                  output norm and gate -> ``xo``, ``crdy``; a CTA in both
+                  ranges runs its unit first
+
+Every CTA issues its o_proj weights after its last role stage's publish
+(``split_roles``, DESIGN_BC 7.2, rule 8: a publish waits for every load in
+flight): a CTA with no role at entry, a split unit after its ``srdy``, a
+combine after its ``crdy``; its core load then polls ``crdy`` with only its own
+weights in flight. Only phase 1 differs between the cores; every stage from
+``stage_o`` on is the same code.
+
+Every hand-off is a tagged pair (5.10/5.11 of the design); the tag carries the
+step epoch the runner bumps once a step and the launch's slot, so nothing is
+zeroed between launches. Every poll waits on a stage earlier in this order on
+some CTA of some rank, and every CTA is resident (one a CU), so the launch
+cannot deadlock; a wait that gives up records itself and fails the rank
+(``sync._spin``), and the launch still completes (every address is clamped).
+
+LDS: the fixed ``red`` and ``RouteLds``, then one union of the stages'
+structs (``lds_structs``); ``xq_ug`` is the sequential composite of
+``load_xq``'s a1 rows and the ug epilogue's buffer, live together from
+``load_xq`` to the last ug task. Every stage that touches the union or ``red``
+ends with a barrier, so the next stage may reuse the bytes.

+"""The contract every Muse Spark MonoKernel package shares: shapes, numerics,
+rows, grid, the K1 / K2 placements, mailbox slots, the build keys, the argument
+lists and the scratch / peer layouts.
+
+Pure Python (``dataclasses`` only): the runtime sizes its buffers and the CPU
+tests check the layouts without torch.cuda or FlyDSL. ``pair_layout`` is the
+K3 helper (``mono.common.plan.pair_layout``) re-implemented here for that
+reason.
+
+Every count is per TP rank of Muse Spark Open at TP8. Every scratch and peer
+offset is sized by ``MAX_TOKENS`` rows (``MAX_PICKS`` picks), never by a
+launch's width, so every width of a step shares one layout and one parity
+half.
+"""
+
+from dataclasses import dataclass
+
+# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
+# The model (Muse Spark Open at TP8)
+
+TP = 8
+HIDDEN = 8192  # H: the residual stream
+MOE_HIDDEN = 4096  # the pooled width the routed experts see
+INTER = 512  # an expert's intermediate a rank (moe_intermediate_size / TP)
+EXPERTS = 256
+TOPK = 8
+EXPERTS_RANK = EXPERTS // TP  # 32 router rows a rank
+HEADS = 16  # query heads a rank (128 / TP)
+KV_HEADS = 2  # KV heads a rank (16 / TP)
+HEAD_DIM = 64
+CORE = HEADS * HEAD_DIM  # 1024: o_proj's K a rank
+
+# runtime.text_shapes(text_config) must equal MUSE_SHAPES, field by field.
+MUSE_SHAPE_FIELDS = (
+    "hidden_size",
+    "num_attention_heads",
+    "num_key_value_heads",
+    "head_dim",
+    "num_local_experts",
+    "num_experts_per_tok",
+    "moe_hidden_size",
+    "moe_intermediate_size",
+    "num_shared_experts",
+    "sliding_window",
+)
+MUSE_SHAPES = (8192, 128, 16, 64, 256, 8, 4096, 4096, 0, 2048)
+
+# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
+# Numerics (refuse_model asserts the loaded modules carry these)
+
+POST_ATTN_EPS = 1e-8  # weightless post_attn_norm
+PRE_FFN_EPS = 1e-5
+PRE_EXP_EPS = 1e-5
+POST_EXP_EPS = 1e-8
+GAIN = 1.0  # fused_gain_center of pre_ffn / pre_expert / post_expert norms
+ROUTE_SCALE = 1.0
+ROUTE_EPS = 1e-15  # router_score_division_eps
+AMAX_FLOOR = 1e-10  # MXFP4 RoundUp: amax = max(amax, AMAX_FLOOR)
+LOG2E = 1.4426950408889634
+
+# Phases B and C (DESIGN_BC section 1.1): the attention front and core.
+RMS_EPS = 1e-5  # pre_qkv_proj_norm, the weightless qk_norm and o_norm
+POST_FFN_EPS = 1e-8  # the previous layer's post_ffn_norm (weight first)
+QK_SCALE_FACTOR = 5.4730064863875  # config.qk_scale_factor
+QK_SCALE = HEAD_DIM**-0.5 * QK_SCALE_FACTOR  # == float(impl.scale)
+QK_SCALE_LOG2E = QK_SCALE * LOG2E  # the split's base-2 logit scale (f32 in-kernel)
+ROPE_THETA = 5e5  # sliding layers' GPT-J RoPE over all 64 dims; full layers: NoPE
+WINDOW = 2048  # sliding layers attend keys L - WINDOW <= k < L
+KV_BLOCK = 16  # tokens a KV page (the kernel block)
+KV_C = 2 * HEAD_DIM  # a (block, head, token) row: K at [0, 64), V at [64, 128)
+V_OFF = HEAD_DIM  # V's element offset in the row
+Q_PER_KV = HEADS // KV_HEADS  # 8 query heads a KV head
+
+# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
+# Rows
+
+MAX_ROWS = 8  # rows a served step has at most (the K3 thread maps)
+MAX_TOKENS = 8  # rows scratch and peer memory are sized for
+MAX_PICKS = MAX_TOKENS * TOPK  # 64 (row, k) picks
+MAX_U = MAX_PICKS  # experts in a step's union
+
+# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
+# Grid: one CTA per CU, all resident
+
+BLOCKS = 256
+THREADS = 512
+WAVES = THREADS // 64  # 8
+LDS_BYTES = 160 * 1024  # a CU's LDS: one CTA's whole
+VGPR_MAX = 256  # arch + acc VGPRs a lane at 2 waves a SIMD
+ROWS = 16  # output rows of a GEMV task (one MFMA tile)
+COLS = 128  # columns of a seam / gather CTA
+
+# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
+# K2 placement (static; section 5.2 of the design)
+
+O_TASKS = HIDDEN // ROWS  # 512 o_proj tasks: CTA b runs b and b + BLOCKS
+NA = HIDDEN // COLS  # 64 seam CTAs [0, NA): 128 columns each
+R0 = 64  # router CTAs [R0, R0 + R_TASKS): one expert row each
+R_TASKS = EXPERTS_RANK  # 32
+P_GROUPS = MOE_HIDDEN // TP // ROWS  # 32 pooler row groups a rank
+P_PARTS = 4  # K quarters of a pooler row group
+P_K = HIDDEN // P_PARTS  # 2048
+P0 = 96  # pooler CTAs [P0, P0 + P_TASKS): g = t // P_PARTS, q = t % P_PARTS
+P_TASKS = P_GROUPS * P_PARTS  # 128
+UG_GROUPS = INTER // 32  # 16 ug tasks a union slot (32 columns each)
+W13_K = MOE_HIDDEN  # 4096
+W13_STEPS = W13_K // 128  # 32 (16 a K half)
+W2_STEPS = INTER // 128  # 4
+DOWN_TASKS = MOE_HIDDEN // ROWS  # 256 == BLOCKS: CTA b owns rows 16b .. 16b + 16
+DOWN_BATCH = 4  # slots of w2 in flight a wave
+OWN_COLS = MOE_HIDDEN // TP  # 512 pooled columns a rank owns (reduce-scatter)
+RED_TASKS = OWN_COLS // ROWS  # 32 owner CTAs [32 rank, 32 rank + 32)
+U_GROUPS = HIDDEN // TP // ROWS  # 64 unpooler row groups a rank
+U_PARTS = 4  # K quarters of an unpooler row group
+U_K = MOE_HIDDEN // U_PARTS  # 1024
+U_TASKS = U_GROUPS * U_PARTS  # 256: CTA b: g = b // U_PARTS, q = b % U_PARTS
+G_TASKS = HIDDEN // COLS  # 64 gather CTAs [0, G_TASKS)
+
+
+def ug_cta0(s: int) -> int:
+    """The first CTA that can get a ug task at S = ``s``: ``run_ug`` gives CTA
+    b the tasks 255 - b, + 256, ... of the step's |U| 16, and |U| <= min(8 S,
+    MAX_U) (only S 8 picks reach the union), so CTA b has a task only if
+    b >= 256 - 16 min(8 S, MAX_U). 128 at S = 1, 0 from S = 2 on."""
+    return max(0, BLOCKS - UG_GROUPS * min(s * TOPK, MAX_U))
+
+
+# MXFP4 activation rows (a1): words a pooled row
+XQ_WORDS = MOE_HIDDEN // 8  # 512 int32 words of packed fp4
+XSC_WORDS = MOE_HIDDEN // 32  # 128 e8m0 codes, one a word in LDS
+
+# LDS route table (common/route_lds.RouteLds): 32-bit words a field
+ROUTE_LDS = dict(
+    route=MAX_TOKENS * 16,  # t*16 + k: id; t*16 + 8 + k: fp32 bits of the weight
+    flag=EXPERTS,
+    expert=MAX_U,
+    kof=MAX_U * 8,
+    scan=WAVES,
+    tot=MAX_TOKENS,
+)
+
+# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
+# K1 placement (Phase B1; DESIGN_BC 5.1): weight-free boundary CTAs [0, NA),
+# the epilogue on CTAs [0, E_UNITS * S), the qkv GEMV on CTAs [NA, BLOCKS)
+
+QKV_ROWS = 2 * CORE + 2 * KV_HEADS * HEAD_DIM  # 2304 a rank: q | k | v | og
+QKV_TILES = QKV_ROWS // ROWS  # 144
+KPARTS = 16  # K parts of a qkv tile
+KPART = HIDDEN // KPARTS  # 512 columns: 4 chunks of 128, one a wave
+K1_TASKS = QKV_TILES * KPARTS  # 2304 (tile, K part) tasks: tau = 16 T + kp
+K1_GEMV0 = NA  # 64: the first GEMV CTA
+K1_GEMV_CTAS = BLOCKS - K1_GEMV0  # 192
+K1_TPC = K1_TASKS // K1_GEMV_CTAS  # 12 tasks a GEMV CTA: tau = 12 g + i
+K1_ROUNDS = K1_TPC // 2  # 6 rounds: waves 0-3 take task 2r, waves 4-7 2r + 1
+K1_MAXC = 2  # GEMV CTAs contributing to a tile
+ROW_Q = 0  # the qkv row blocks: q heads, k heads, v heads, o_gate heads
+ROW_K = CORE
+ROW_V = ROW_K + KV_HEADS * HEAD_DIM
+ROW_G = ROW_V + KV_HEADS * HEAD_DIM
+E_UNITS = 5  # epilogue units a token: q 0-7, q 8-15, k + v, og 0-7, og 8-15
+
+
+def k1_contributor0(tile: int) -> int:
+    """The first of the ``K1_MAXC`` GEMV CTAs (g = b - K1_GEMV0) whose tasks
+    cover ``tile``: contributor c = g - k1_contributor0(tile) holds a run of the
+    tile's K parts, c = 0 the lower ones."""
+    return (KPARTS * tile) // K1_TPC
+
+
+assert K1_TASKS == K1_TPC * K1_GEMV_CTAS and ROWS * QKV_TILES == QKV_ROWS
+assert ROW_G + CORE == QKV_ROWS and KPART * KPARTS == HIDDEN and KPART == 4 * COLS
+assert E_UNITS * MAX_ROWS <= NA and K1_ROUNDS * 2 == K1_TPC
+
+# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
+# K2 split-KV core placement (Phase C, q = 1 widths; DESIGN_BC 7.1). Split
+# unit u = (t * 2 + kvh) * N + p runs on CTA u; combine (t, h) on CTA
+# C0(S) + 16 t + h. A CTA holding both runs its unit first.
+
+NSPLIT_SW = 9  # sliding: <= 129 pages a window -> <= 9 live units
+MIN_PER = 16  # pages a live unit at least: two a wave (two in flight)
+
+
+def nsplit(S: int, window: bool) -> int:
+    """N: units a (token, KV head) (DESIGN_BC 7.1)."""
+    return NSPLIT_SW if window else BLOCKS // (2 * S)
+
+
+def n_units(S: int, window: bool) -> int:
+    """Split units of a launch (CTAs [0, n_units))."""
+    return 2 * S * nsplit(S, window)
+
+
+def n_comb(S: int) -> int:
+    """Combine CTAs of a launch: one a (token, q head), 16 S."""
+    return HEADS * S
+
+
+def C0(S: int) -> int:
+    """The first combine CTA: [C0, BLOCKS) runs one (token, q head) each."""
+    return BLOCKS - n_comb(S)
+
+
+assert all(
+    n_units(s, w) <= BLOCKS and C0(s) >= BLOCKS // 2
+    for s in range(1, MAX_ROWS + 1)
+    for w in (False, True)
+)
+
+# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
+# Mailbox tags: tag = (epoch & EPOCH_MASK) * TAG_SLOTS + slot + 1
+
+EPOCH_MASK = (1 << 22) - 1  # kernels use e & EPOCH_MASK: the int32 epoch may wrap
+TAG_SLOTS = 256
+K1_SLOT0 = 0  # Phase B's K1 launches
+K2_SLOT0 = 128  # K2 launches
+
+
+def k1_slot(layer_idx: int) -> int:
+    """The tag slot of a layer's K1 launch (Phase B)."""
+    if not 0 <= layer_idx < K2_SLOT0 - K1_SLOT0:
+        raise ValueError(f"layer {layer_idx} has no K1 slot")
+    return K1_SLOT0 + layer_idx
+
+
+def k2_slot(layer_idx: int) -> int:
+    """The tag slot of a layer's K2 launch."""
+    if not 0 <= layer_idx < TAG_SLOTS - K2_SLOT0:
+        raise ValueError(f"layer {layer_idx} has no K2 slot")
+    return K2_SLOT0 + layer_idx
+
+
+def step_tag(epoch: int, slot: int) -> int:
+    """The host mirror of ``sync.step_tag``: the tag every pair a launch of
+    ``slot`` writes at ``epoch`` carries (two's complement ``&``, so a wrapped,
+    negative int32 epoch gives the kernel's tag too). Never 0: a zeroed pair is
+    never current."""
+    return (epoch & EPOCH_MASK) * TAG_SLOTS + slot + 1
+
+
+assert P0 + P_TASKS <= BLOCKS and R0 + R_TASKS <= P0 and NA <= R0
+assert DOWN_TASKS == BLOCKS and U_TASKS == BLOCKS and O_TASKS == 2 * BLOCKS
+assert RED_TASKS * TP == DOWN_TASKS and MAX_ROWS <= MAX_TOKENS <= 8
+assert G_TASKS <= BLOCKS and MAX_U <= EXPERTS and TOPK <= 8
+assert step_tag(EPOCH_MASK, TAG_SLOTS - 1) < 2**31  # a tag is a positive int32

+# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
+# The build keys and the argument lists
+
+K2_CORES = ("tensor", "gated", "split")  # K2Build.core
+_CORE_SUFFIX = {"tensor": "", "gated": "_g"}  # split: "_sw" / "_full"
+
+
+def _check_key(key, ints: tuple[str, ...], bools: tuple[str, ...]) -> None:
+    """The fields ``ints`` / ``bools`` typed, the width in range, and the fault
+    hook complete and able to fire in a K2 launch."""
+    cls = type(key).__name__
+    for f in ints:
+        v = getattr(key, f)
+        if type(v) is not int:  # bool too: it would name the symbol "sTrue"
+            raise TypeError(f"{cls}.{f} = {v!r}: an int")
+    for f in bools:
+        v = getattr(key, f)
+        if type(v) is not bool:
+            raise TypeError(f"{cls}.{f} = {v!r}: a bool")
+    if not 1 <= key.tokens <= MAX_ROWS:
+        raise ValueError(f"{cls}.tokens {key.tokens} (1 .. {MAX_ROWS})")
+    if isinstance(key, K1Build):
+        return
+    if not -1 <= key.fault_rank < TP:
+        raise ValueError(f"{cls}.fault_rank {key.fault_rank} (-1 .. {TP - 1})")
+    if not key.faulty:
+        # One build, one key: the fault fields of a build without the hook
+        # would key a second binary under the same kernel name.
+        if (key.fault_epoch, key.fault_slot, key.fault_ticks) != (0, 0, 0):
+            raise ValueError(f"{cls}.fault_* set without fault_rank")
+        return
+    # sync.stall compares these with the int32 epoch word and the slot
+    # argument: an epoch past int32 or a slot this kernel never runs never fires.
+    if not 0 <= key.fault_epoch < 2**31:
+        raise ValueError(f"{cls}.fault_epoch {key.fault_epoch} (0 .. 2^31 - 1)")
+    if not K2_SLOT0 <= key.fault_slot < TAG_SLOTS:
+        raise ValueError(
+            f"{cls}.fault_slot {key.fault_slot}: a K2 slot "
+            f"({K2_SLOT0} .. {TAG_SLOTS - 1}, spec.k2_slot)"
+        )
+    if not 0 < key.fault_ticks < 2**63:
+        raise ValueError(f"{cls}.fault_ticks {key.fault_ticks} (> 0)")

+def _fault_suffix(key) -> str:
+    if not key.faulty:
+        return ""
+    return f"_f{key.fault_rank}_{key.fault_epoch}_{key.fault_slot}_{key.fault_ticks}"

+    # once, in the launch of slot fault_slot of the step at epoch fault_epoch.
+    fault_rank: int = -1
+    fault_epoch: int = 0
+    fault_slot: int = 0
+    fault_ticks: int = 0
+    # The attention core K2 reads (K2_CORES): "tensor" o_proj's input from
+    # vLLM (Phase A), "gated" vLLM's attention output and the qkv rows, the
+    # gated norm in the core load (B2), "split" the split-KV core in-kernel
+    # (C, q = 1 widths).
+    core: str = "tensor"
+    window: bool = False  # split only: a sliding layer's key window
+
+    def __post_init__(self):
+        _check_key(
+            self,
+            ("tokens", "fault_rank", "fault_epoch", "fault_slot", "fault_ticks"),
+            ("window",),
+        )
+        if type(self.core) is not str:
+            raise TypeError(f"K2Build.core = {self.core!r}: a str")
+        if self.core not in K2_CORES:
+            raise ValueError(f"K2Build.core {self.core!r} (one of {K2_CORES})")
+        if self.window and self.core != "split":
+            raise ValueError(f"K2Build.window with core {self.core!r} (split only)")
+
+    @property
+    def faulty(self) -> bool:
+        """The build compiles ``sync.stall`` into its prologue."""
+        return self.fault_rank >= 0
+
+    def nsplit(self) -> int:
+        """A split build's N: units a (token, KV head)."""
+        return nsplit(self.tokens, self.window)
+
+    def n_units(self) -> int:
+        """A split build's units (CTAs [0, n_units))."""
+        return n_units(self.tokens, self.window)
+
+    def c0(self) -> int:
+        """A split build's first combine CTA."""
+        return C0(self.tokens)
+
+    def kernel_name(self) -> str:
+        """The kernel symbol: one per build. A Phase A build ("tensor") keeps
+        its Phase A name."""
+        if self.core == "split":
+            core = "_sw" if self.window else "_full"
+        else:
+            core = _CORE_SUFFIX[self.core]
+        return f"muse_mono_k2_s{self.tokens}{core}" + _fault_suffix(self)
+
+
+@dataclass(frozen=True)
+class K1Build:
+    """Every K1 build parameter (Phase B1: the residual boundary, the qkv GEMV,
+    QK-norm / RoPE and the KV insert of one layer), scalars only. One template;
+    ``rope`` is the only difference between the two attention kinds."""
+
+    tokens: int  # S, the launch's rows: 1 .. MAX_ROWS
+    rope: bool  # a sliding layer's GPT-J RoPE (full layers: NoPE)
+
+    def __post_init__(self):
+        _check_key(self, ("tokens",), ("rope",))
+
+    def kernel_name(self) -> str:
+        """The kernel symbol: one per build."""
+        kind = "rope" if self.rope else "nope"
+        return f"muse_mono_k1_s{self.tokens}_{kind}"
+
+
+K2_ARGS = (
+    "core",  # bf16 [S, CORE]: o_proj's input
+    "stream",  # fp32 [S, HIDDEN]: the residual stream
+    "pad",  # bool [>= S]: pad rows

+    "attn_alpha",
+    "attn_beta",
+    "w_preffn",
+    "w_router",
+    "bias",
+    "w_pool",
+    "w_preexp",
+    "w13",
+    "w13s",
+    "w2",
+    "w2s",
+    "w_postexp",
+    "w_unpool",
+    "stream_out",  # fp32 [S, HIDDEN]
+    "branch_out",  # bf16 [S, HIDDEN]
+    "scratch",
+    "peers",  # int64 [TP]: every rank's peer buffer past PEER_HEAD
+    "rank",
+    "epoch",
+    "slot",
+    "health",
+    "alarm",
+)
+
+# K2's arguments by K2Build.core: "gated" reads vLLM's attention output and the
+# qkv rows (og at ROW_G) in place of ``core``; "split" reads the qkv rows, this
+# layer's KV cache and its KV group's block table and sequence lengths. The
+# launch state (the last 7) is every core's.
+K2_KV_ARGS = (
+    "kv",  # bf16 [blocks, KV_HEADS, KV_BLOCK, KV_C]: the layer's cache
+    "kv_sb",  # byte strides of a block, a head, a token (Int64)
+    "kv_sh",
+    "kv_st",
+    "kv_blocks",  # Int32: the cache's blocks (block ids are clamped below it)
+)
+K2_ARGS_BY_CORE = {
+    "tensor": K2_ARGS,
+    "gated": (
+        "attn",  # bf16 [S, CORE]: the stock core's output, contiguous
+        "qkvo",  # bf16 [S, QKV_ROWS]: the qkv rows (og at ROW_G)
+        *K2_ARGS[1:],
+    ),
+    "split": (
+        "qkvo",  # bf16 [S, QKV_ROWS]: q normalized and roped, og raw
+        *K2_KV_ARGS,
+        "block_table",  # int32 [bt_rows, bt_stride]: the KV group's (persistent)
+        "bt_rows",  # Int32: the table's rows (its buffer's size)
+        "bt_stride",  # Int32: the table's row stride in entries
+        "seq_lens",  # int32 [>= S]: context lengths, this step's token included
+        *K2_ARGS[1:],
+    ),
+}
+
+K1_ARGS = (
+    "branch",  # bf16 [S, HIDDEN]: the previous layer's deferred branch
+    "stream",  # fp32 [S, HIDDEN]: the residual stream
+    "pad",  # bool [>= S]: pad rows
+    "positions",  # int64 [>= S]
+    "slots",  # int64 [>= S]: this layer's slot mapping (< 0: no insert)
+    "w_postffn",  # layer i - 1: post_ffn_norm.weight bf16
+    "ffn_alpha",  # layer i - 1: add_ffn alpha / beta fp32
+    "ffn_beta",
+    "w_preqkv",  # layer i: pre_qkv_proj_norm.weight bf16
+    "w_qkv",  # layer i: qkv_proj.weight bf16 [QKV_ROWS, HIDDEN]
+    "cos_sin",  # layer i: rotary cos_sin_cache fp32 [max_pos, 64] (0 if NoPE)

+    "stream_out",  # fp32 [S, HIDDEN]: K2's stream
+    "qkvo",  # bf16 [S, QKV_ROWS]: the qkv rows after QK-norm / RoPE
+    "scratch",
+    "rank",  # no peers: K1 is rank-local; stall() compares the rank
+    "epoch",
+    "slot",
+    "health",
+    "alarm",

+# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
+# Scratch and peer layouts (section 5.10 of the design)
+
+PAIR_BYTES = 8  # a (value, tag) int32 pair
+
+# Mailbox regions, in layout order; then debug.region_ids order (wait records).
+SCRATCH_REGIONS = (
+    "xrdy",
+    "ass",
+    "bss",
+    "ppart",
+    "route",
+    "inter",
+    "isc",
+    "upart",
+)
+PEER_REGIONS = ("ar", "rlog", "pool", "rsx", "sqx", "moe", "branch")
+# Plain (untagged) scratch regions, after the mailboxes.
+XROW = "xrow"  # bf16 [MAX_TOKENS, HIDDEN]: ffn_in rows (seam -> router, pooler)
+XROW_ALIGN = 16  # dwordx4 loads
+
+_MT, _MP = MAX_TOKENS, MAX_PICKS
+SCRATCH_PAIRS = (
+    ("xrdy", NA),  # j: seam slice j published (flag)
+    ("ass", NA * _MT),  # j*MT + t: fp32 sum of attn_out^2 over slice j
+    ("bss", NA * _MT),  # j*MT + t: fp32 sum of new_stream^2 over slice j
+    ("ppart", P_GROUPS * (P_PARTS - 1) * _MT * ROWS),  # ((g*3 + q-1)*MT + t)*16 + r
+    ("route", _MT * 16),  # t*16 + k: id; t*16 + 8 + k: fp32 weight
+    ("inter", _MP * 64),  # pick*64 + 4g + w: a2 fp4 words
+    ("isc", _MP * UG_GROUPS),  # pick*16 + g: a2 e8m0 code
+    (None, RED_TASKS * _MP),  # reserved (the retired rank-local ``pss``)
+    ("upart", U_GROUPS * (U_PARTS - 1) * _MT * ROWS),  # ((g*3 + q-1)*MT + t)*16 + r
+)
+# Reserved bytes before ``xrow`` (a retired debug region): kept so that every
+# later offset, compiled into the kernels as an immediate, stays (as the
+# reserved pairs of the retired ``pss`` above).
+RESERVED_A = _MT * (XQ_WORDS + XSC_WORDS) * PAIR_BYTES
+XROW_BYTES = _MT * HIDDEN * 2
+
+# Phases B and C (DESIGN_BC 5.7): mailboxes, then plain regions, laid out past
+# ``xrow`` so that every Phase A offset (and every Phase A K2 binary) stays.
+SCRATCH_PAIRS_BC = (
+    ("fss", NA * _MT),  # j*MT + t: K1 boundary, fp32 sum of x^2 over slice j
+    ("nss", NA * _MT),  # j*MT + t: fp32 sum of new_stream^2 over slice j
+    ("ardy", NA),  # j: K1 boundary slice j's arow published (flag)
+    ("qpart", QKV_TILES * K1_MAXC * _MT * ROWS),  # ((T*2 + c)*MT + t)*16 + r
+    ("srdy", BLOCKS),  # u: split unit u's opart / pstat published (flag)
+    ("crdy", 16 * _MT),  # 16 t + h: combine (t, h)'s xo row published (flag)
+)
+SCRATCH_REGIONS_BC = tuple(n for n, _ in SCRATCH_PAIRS_BC)
+SCRATCH_REGIONS_ALL = SCRATCH_REGIONS + SCRATCH_REGIONS_BC
+# Every region a wait record may name (debug.region_ids; ids are name CRCs, so
+# the order is free).
+REGIONS = SCRATCH_REGIONS_ALL + PEER_REGIONS
+
+# Plain (untagged) regions past the B/C mailboxes: (name, bytes, alignment).
+AROW = "arow"  # bf16 [MT, HIDDEN]: K1's attn_in rows (boundary -> GEMV)
+XO = "xo"  # bf16 [MT, CORE]: the split core's gated rows (combine -> load_core)
+PSTAT = "pstat"  # fp32 [BLOCKS, 8, 2]: a split unit's (m, l) per q head
+OPART = "opart"  # fp32 [BLOCKS, 8, HEAD_DIM]: a split unit's unnormalized rows
+SCRATCH_PLAIN_BC = (
+    (AROW, _MT * HIDDEN * 2, 16),
+    (None, _MT * QKV_ROWS * 2, 16),  # reserved (a retired debug region)
+    (XO, _MT * CORE * 2, 16),
+    (PSTAT, BLOCKS * Q_PER_KV * 2 * 4, 16),
+    (OPART, BLOCKS * Q_PER_KV * HEAD_DIM * 4, 16),
+)
+
+# One parity half; pair indexes are in the reader's buffer.
+PEER_PAIRS = (
+    ("ar", TP * _MT * HIDDEN // 2),  # ((src*MT + t)*8192 + col)/2: bf16 partials
+    ("rlog", TP * _MT * EXPERTS_RANK),  # (src*MT + t)*32 + i: fp32 logits
+    ("pool", _MT * MOE_HIDDEN // 2),  # (t*4096 + col)/2: bf16 pooled
+    ("rsx", TP * _MP * OWN_COLS // 2),  # ((src*MP + pick)*512 + cc)/2: bf16 rows
+    ("sqx", TP * _MP * RED_TASKS),  # (src*MP + pick)*32 + j: fp32 sum x^2, 16 cols
+    ("moe", _MT * MOE_HIDDEN // 2),  # (t*4096 + col)/2: bf16 MoE output
+    ("branch", _MT * HIDDEN // 2),  # (t*8192 + col)/2: bf16 unpooler output
+)
+
+
+def pair_layout(items, align: int = PAIR_BYTES, start: int = 0) -> dict:
+    """``items`` (name, pairs) laid out in order: name -> (byte offset, bytes),
+    each region from an ``align``-byte boundary at or past ``start``; a None
+    name reserves its pairs."""
+    out, off = {}, start
+    for name, pairs in items:
+        off = (off + align - 1) // align * align
+        if name is not None:
+            out[name] = (off, pairs * PAIR_BYTES)
+        off += pairs * PAIR_BYTES
+    return out
+
+
+def _end(layout: dict) -> int:
+    return max(off + size for off, size in layout.values())
+
+
+def _align(off: int, align: int) -> int:
+    return (off + align - 1) // align * align
+
+
+def scratch_layout() -> dict[str, tuple[int, int]]:
+    """A rank's scratch (one buffer shared by every launch of a step; the tags
+    tell launches apart): the mailboxes, ``RESERVED_A`` bytes, then ``xrow``
+    (16-byte aligned); then Phases B / C's mailboxes and plain regions.
+    name -> (byte offset, bytes)."""
+    out = pair_layout(SCRATCH_PAIRS)
+    out[XROW] = (_align(_end(out) + RESERVED_A, XROW_ALIGN), XROW_BYTES)
+    out.update(pair_layout(SCRATCH_PAIRS_BC, start=_end(out)))
+    off = _end(out)
+    for name, nbytes, align in SCRATCH_PLAIN_BC:
+        off = _align(off, align)
+        if name is not None:
+            out[name] = (off, nbytes)
+        off += nbytes
+    return out
+
+
+def scratch_bytes() -> int:
+    return _end(scratch_layout())
+
+
+def peer_layout() -> dict[str, tuple[int, int]]:
+    """One parity half of a rank's peer buffer: name -> (byte offset, bytes).
+    The kernels see the buffer past ``abi.PEER_HEAD``; parity ``e & 1`` adds
+    ``e & 1`` halves."""
+    return pair_layout(PEER_PAIRS)
+
+
+def peer_half_bytes() -> int:
+    return _end(peer_layout())
+
+
+def peer_bytes() -> int:
+    """Both parity halves; ``abi.PEER_HEAD`` is not included."""
+    return 2 * peer_half_bytes()
+
+
+# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
+# Pair indexes (section 5.10): pair units for put / put_words / poll; put_bf
+# takes the element index 2 * pair. Plain integer arithmetic, so the host tests
+# and the kernels' traced Int32 math read the same formulas.
+
+
+def ar_pair(src, t, col):
+    return ((src * _MT + t) * HIDDEN + col) // 2
+
+
+def rlog_pair(src, t, i):
+    return (src * _MT + t) * EXPERTS_RANK + i
+
+
+def pool_pair(t, col):
+    return (t * MOE_HIDDEN + col) // 2
+
+
+def rsx_pair(src, pick, cc):
+    return ((src * _MP + pick) * OWN_COLS + cc) // 2
+
+
+def sqx_pair(src, j, pick):
+    """Owner CTA j of rank src's 16-column sum of squares of ``pick``: a
+    rank's 32 slices of a pick adjacent (a lane loads 4 as two 2-pair specs)."""
+    return (src * _MP + pick) * RED_TASKS + j
+
+
+def moe_pair(t, col):
+    return (t * MOE_HIDDEN + col) // 2
+
+
+def branch_pair(t, col):
+    return (t * HIDDEN + col) // 2
+
+
+def xrdy_pair(j):
+    return j
+
+
+def ss_pair(j, t):
+    """``ass`` and ``bss`` (K2's seam); ``fss`` and ``nss`` (K1's boundary)."""
+    return j * _MT + t
+
+
+def ppart_pair(g, q, t, r):
+    return ((g * (P_PARTS - 1) + q - 1) * _MT + t) * ROWS + r
+
+
+def route_id_pair(t, k):
+    return t * 16 + k
+
+
+def route_weight_pair(t, k):
+    return t * 16 + 8 + k
+
+
+def upart_pair(g, q, t, r):
+    return ((g * (U_PARTS - 1) + q - 1) * _MT + t) * ROWS + r
+
+
+def ardy_pair(j):
+    return j
+
+
+def qpart_pair(T, c, t, r):
+    """K1: contributor c's partial of qkv tile T's row r for token t."""
+    return ((T * K1_MAXC + c) * _MT + t) * ROWS + r
+
+
+def srdy_pair(u):
+    return u
+
+
+def crdy_pair(t, h):
+    return 16 * t + h
+
+
+# Plain (untagged) regions: word / element indexes from the region's base.
+
+
+def xrow_elem(t, col):
+    """``xrow`` bf16 element of row t, column col."""
+    return t * HIDDEN + col
+
+
+def arow_elem(t, col):
+    """``arow`` bf16 element of row t, column col."""
+    return t * HIDDEN + col
+
+
+def xo_elem(t, h, d):
+    """``xo`` bf16 element of token t, q head h, dim d."""
+    return t * CORE + HEAD_DIM * h + d
+
+
+def pstat_word(u, j, k):
+    """``pstat`` fp32 word of split unit u, its q head j (of 8), k = 0: the
+    running max m (base 2), k = 1: the sum l."""
+    return (u * Q_PER_KV + j) * 2 + k
+
+
+def opart_word(u, j, d):
+    """``opart`` fp32 word of split unit u, its q head j, dim d."""
+    return (u * Q_PER_KV + j) * HEAD_DIM + d

+"""K2 phase 3b: the routed experts of one Muse Spark layer and rank, from the
+MXFP4 pre-expert-normed pooled rows (``xq`` / ``xsc`` in LDS, ``pool.load_xq``)
+to every pick's bf16 rows pushed to their column owner (``rsx``).
+
+Adapted from K3's latent MoE (pr60683 ``kimi_k3/amd/specialized_decode/mono/
+stages/moe.py``: ``load_route``, ``ug_loads`` / ``stage_ug``, ``load_inter``,
+``down_loads`` / ``stage_down``) to Muse's shapes (256 experts, top-8, I_local
+512, pooled K 4096), its stage-1 numerics (aiter's SiLU, a bf16 h, the RoundUp
+MXFP4 a2) and its reduce (unweighted rows, reduced by the column owner).
+
+    union  (every CTA, ``load_route``): ROUTE -> the LDS route table; the union U
+           of the step's live picks (``0 <= id < 256``; pad rows carry -1, a
+           garbage id after a timed-out poll is dead too): ``slot_of[e]``,
+           ``expert[slot]`` ascending (zeroed past |U|), ``kof[slot 8 + t]``
+    ug     (|U| x 16 tasks, every CTA, reversed placement, ``run_ug``): 32 gate +
+           32 up rows of a slot's expert against the MXFP4 rows (FP4 x FP4
+           scaled MFMA, K halves on waves 0-3 / 4-7), SiLU (aiter: hw exp2 /
+           rcp), h rounded to bf16, MXFP4 a 32-column group (RoundUp) ->
+           INTER / ISC of each picking row
+    down   (CTA b: 16 of the 4096 pooled rows, ``run_down``): w2 of every slot
+           against its picks' INTER (live picks only polled) -> a bf16 row a
+           pick, UNWEIGHTED (the post-expert norm comes before the route weight)
+           -> the owner rank's RSX (``b // 32``), zeros included
+
+Pad rule: a dead pick (pad row, garbage id) is never in U and never polled; its
+contribution rows stay the zeros ``load_inter`` stores (``select``, never a mask
+multiply). Every expert id is clamped into [0, 256) and every slot into
+[0, MAX_U) at each address use, so a timed-out step keeps its addresses in
+bounds. A dead slot or task (past |U|) loads expert 256 instead, one past the
+sized w13 / w2 resources (``_expert_or_past``): out of range, its loads return
+zeros without a memory request, and its MFMAs are skipped. Every stage here
+touching the stage LDS or ``red`` ends with a barrier (the LDS hand-over rule).
+"""
+

+from aiter.ops.flydsl.kernels import buffer_ops as bo
+from flydsl.expr import gpu, range_constexpr
+from flydsl.expr.typing import T

+from vllm.models.muse_spark.amd.specialized_decode.mono.common.ranks import peer_at
+from vllm.models.muse_spark.amd.specialized_decode.mono.common.route_lds import (
+    clamp_expert,

+HALF_STEPS = W13_STEPS // 2  # 16 K steps a ug wave (its K half)
+W13_ROWS = 2 * INTER  # an expert's w13 rows: gate 512 | up 512
+W13_EXPERT_DWORDS = W13_ROWS * W13_K // 8  # 524288: an expert's fp4 w13
+W2_EXPERT_DWORDS = MOE_HIDDEN * INTER // 8  # 262144: an expert's fp4 w2
+W2_SCALE_COLS = INTER // 32  # 16 e8m0 codes a w2 row
+INTER_WORDS = INTER // 8  # 64 fp4 words of a pick's a2 row
+UP_GROUP0 = INTER // ROWS  # 32: the first up row group of an expert

+# their buffer resources, expert EXPERTS past the end
+W13_BYTES = EXPERTS * W13_EXPERT_DWORDS * 4

+_LAY = scratch_layout()

+ISC_FROM_ROUTE = (_LAY["isc"][0] - _LAY["route"][0]) // PAIR_BYTES

+assert INTER_WORDS == 64 and THREADS % INTER_WORDS == 0
+assert ISC_FROM_ROUTE > 0 and (_LAY["isc"][0] - _LAY["route"][0]) % PAIR_BYTES == 0

+assert all(

+    == 2 * (st % 2) + rgd % 2
+    for rgd in range(4)
+    for r in range(16)
+    for st in range(W2_STEPS)
+    for kb in range(4)

+def ug_lds_struct(s: int):
+    """The ug epilogue's buffer: ``av`` f32[THREADS], a (row, column) thread's bf16
+    h, read back 8 at a time for the fp4 pack. K2 lays it out after
+    ``pool.xq_lds_struct`` (the ``xq_ug`` composite: both live through the ug
+    tasks)."""
+    if s not in _UG_LDS:
+
+        @fx.struct
+        class UgLds:
+            av: fx.Array[fx.Float32, THREADS, 16]
+
+        _UG_LDS[s] = UgLds
+    return _UG_LDS[s]
+
+
+def down_lds_struct(s: int):
+    """The down stage's operands: ``interq`` (a pick's 64 a2 words), ``intsc`` (its 16
+    codes) and ``contrib`` (its 16 bf16-rounded rows of this CTA), s 8 picks."""
+    if s not in _DOWN_LDS:

+        @fx.struct
+        class DownLds:
+            interq: fx.Array[fx.Int32, s * TOPK * INTER_WORDS, 16]
+            intsc: fx.Array[fx.Int32, s * TOPK * UG_GROUPS, 16]

+# ---------------------------------------------------------------- indexes
+# Plain integer arithmetic: the kernels' traced Int32 math and the host tests
+# read the same formulas.

+def inter_word(pick, g, w):
+    """``inter`` pair of a pick's a2 word w (columns 32 g + 8 w .. + 8) of
+    32-column group g."""
+    return pick * INTER_WORDS + 4 * g + w
+
+
+def inter_read_word(pick, st, kb, d):
+    """The a2 word a down lane (K block ``kb`` = lane / 16) feeds its MFMA at
+    128-K step ``st``: the K order of w2's ``fp4_tile_load`` (K 128 st + 32 kb
+    + 8 d ..)."""
+    return pick * INTER_WORDS + 16 * st + 4 * kb + d
+
+
+def isc_index(pick, g):
+    """``isc`` pair of a pick's group-g a2 code."""
+    return pick * UG_GROUPS + g
+
+
+def xq_read_word(t, st, kb, d):
+    """The a1 word (``pool.load_xq``'s ``xq[t 512 + kb' 4 + w]``, kb' the
+    32-column block) a ug lane feeds its MFMA at step ``st``, K block ``kb``."""
+    return t * XQ_WORDS + 16 * st + 4 * kb + d
+
+
+def ug_row_group(wave, g):
+    """The w13 16-row group wave ``wave`` multiplies for 32-column group ``g``:
+    waves 0 / 4 gate rows 32 g .., 1 / 5 gate 32 g + 16 .., 2 / 6 up rows
+    512 + 32 g .., 3 / 7 up 512 + 32 g + 16 .. (a 32-row scale block holds two
+    gate or two up groups, never one of each)."""
+    rgl = wave % 4
+    return (rgl // 2) * UP_GROUP0 + 2 * g + rgl % 2
+
+
+def rsx_elem(rank, pick, rgd, rp):
+    """``put_bf`` element index of down CTA ``rgd``'s column pair ``rp`` of a
+    pick in its owner's ``rsx`` (2 ``spec.rsx_pair``)."""
+    return (rank * MAX_PICKS + pick) * OWN_COLS + (rgd % RED_TASKS) * ROWS + 2 * rp
+
+
+def slot_expert(c, slot):
+    """Union slot ``slot``'s expert id, wave-uniform, the slot clamped into
+    [0, MAX_U) and the id into [0, EXPERTS): an in-bounds weight address for
+    any slot (past |U| ``expert`` holds 0) or garbage id."""
+    sl = fx.max(fx.min(slot, MAX_U - 1), 0)
+    return clamp_expert(uniform(fx.ptr_load(c["rt"]["expert"] + sl)))
+
+
+def _expert_or_past(c, slot, nu):
+    """``slot_expert`` of a live slot (``slot < nu``), else EXPERTS: the dead
+    slot's weight and scale loads land past the sized resources (out of range:
+    zeros, no memory request). Wave-uniform."""
+    return (slot < nu).select(slot_expert(c, slot), fx.Int32(EXPERTS))
+
+
+def down_width(s):
+    """The slots of a ``stage_down`` batch at S rows: |U| <= min(8 S, MAX_U)
+    (``load_route`` counts the distinct live ids of the S 8 picks) over the 8
+    waves, at most DOWN_BATCH (S = 1: one slot a wave)."""
+    return min(DOWN_BATCH, cdiv(min(s * TOPK, MAX_U), WAVES))
+
+
+def _pick_id(rt, pick):
+    """The expert id of pick ``pick`` = t 8 + k in the LDS route table."""
+    return fx.ptr_load(rt["route"] + id_index(pick // TOPK, pick % TOPK))
+
+
+def _live(e):
+    return (e >= 0) & (e < EXPERTS)
+
+
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------- union
+
+
+@traced
+def load_route(c):
+    """ROUTE -> the LDS route table (ids, weight bits) and the union U of the
+    live picks: ``flag[e]`` (U's slot of e), ``expert[slot]`` (ascending, 0
+    past |U|), ``kof[slot 8 + t]`` (row t's top-k index of the slot's expert,
+    -1 when t did not pick it). LDS is not zeroed at launch: every field read
+    later is written here first. Returns |U| (wave-uniform), 0 when every row
+    is a pad."""
+    s, tid, lane, wave = c["S"], c["tid"], c["lane"], c["wave"]
+    rt = c["rt"]
+    tid32 = fx.Int32(tid)
+    if tid < s * 16:
+        v = c["poll"]([(c["scr"]["route"], tid32, 1)])[0][0]
+        fx.ptr_store(v, rt["route"] + tid32)
+    if tid < EXPERTS:
+        fx.ptr_store(fx.Int32(0), rt["flag"] + tid32)
+    if tid < MAX_U:
+        fx.ptr_store(fx.Int32(0), rt["expert"] + tid32)
+    fx.ptr_store(fx.Int32(-1), rt["kof"] + tid32)  # MAX_U 8 == THREADS words
+    gpu.barrier()
+    if tid < s * TOPK:
+        e = _pick_id(rt, tid32)
+        if _live(e):
+            fx.ptr_store(fx.Int32(1), rt["flag"] + clamp_expert(e))

+        fx.ptr_load(rt["flag"] + fx.min(tid32, EXPERTS - 1)), fx.Int32(0)
+    )
+    off, tot = block_excl_scan(f, lane, wave, rt["scan"])
+    gpu.barrier()  # every flag read before a slot overwrites one
+    if f == 1:
+        fx.ptr_store(off, rt["flag"] + tid32)
+        fx.ptr_store(tid32, rt["expert"] + fx.min(off, MAX_U - 1))
+    gpu.barrier()

+        e = _pick_id(rt, tid32)
+        if _live(e):
+            sl = fx.min(fx.ptr_load(rt["flag"] + clamp_expert(e)), MAX_U - 1)

+    gpu.barrier()

+# ---------------------------------------------------------------- ug

+def ug_loads(c, task, nu):
+    """Task ``task``'s w13 operands for this wave (its row group, its K half:
+    16 dwordx4) and their scale words (8: a word serves 2 steps x 2 row
+    groups), issued a task ahead (``stage_ug`` takes them). A task past the
+    step's last (its slot past |U| = ``nu``) loads zeros (``_expert_or_past``)."""
+    lane, wave = c["lane"], c["wave"]
+    a = c["args"]
+    e = _expert_or_past(c, task // UG_GROUPS, nu)
+    rg = ug_row_group(wave, task % UG_GROUPS)
+    st0 = (wave // 4) * HALF_STEPS
+    r_w = rsrc(a["w13"], W13_BYTES)
+    base = e * W13_EXPERT_DWORDS
+    av = [
+        fp4_tile_load(r_w, base, rg, W13_K, st0 + i, lane * 4)
+        for i in range(HALF_STEPS)
+    ]
+    r_s = rsrc(a["w13s"], W13S_BYTES)
+    sw = [
+        fx.Int32(
+            bo.buffer_load(
+                r_s, w13_scale_word(e, rg, st0 + i, lane), vec_width=1, dtype=T.i32
+            )
+        )
+        for i in range(0, HALF_STEPS, 2)
+    ]
+    return av + sw
+
+
+@traced
+def stage_ug(c, task, ops):
+    """Slot task / 16, 32-column group g = task % 16: the gate rows 32 g .. and
+    up rows 512 + 32 g .. of the slot's expert (``ops``: ``ug_loads``) against

+    rcp), the 32-column group's RoundUp code, the fp4 pack -> INTER / ISC of
+    every row that picked the expert."""
+    s, tid, lane, wave, red = c["S"], c["tid"], c["lane"], c["wave"], c["red"]
+    rt, xq = c["rt"], c["lds"]["xq"]
+    av_l = c["lds"]["ug"]["av"]
+    slot = fx.max(fx.min(task // UG_GROUPS, MAX_U - 1), 0)
+    g = task % UG_GROUPS
+    rg = ug_row_group(wave, g)
+    st0 = (wave // 4) * HALF_STEPS
+    t = fx.min(lane % 16, s - 1)
+    kb = lane // 16
+    acc = fx.Vector.filled(4, 0.0, fx.Float32)
+    for i in range_constexpr(HALF_STEPS):
+        st = st0 + i
+        bw = fx.Vector(
+            fx.ptr_load(
+                xq["xq"] + xq_read_word(t, st, kb, 0),
+                result_type=fx.Vector.make_type(4, fx.Int32),
+            )
+        )
+        sb = fx.ptr_load(xq["xsc"] + (t * XSC_WORDS + st * 4 + kb))
+        # the code's byte (st % 2) 2 + rg % 2 of the word (st % 2 == i % 2)
+        sa = (ops[HALF_STEPS + i // 2] >> ((i % 2) * 16 + (rg % 2) * 8)) & 0xFF

+    col = tid % 32
+    on = tt < s
+    tt = fx.min(tt, s - 1)
+    first = col < 16  # row group 2 g (waves 0 / 2, + 4 the K's 2nd half) or 2 g + 1
+    r = col % 16
+    gv = first.select(
+        row_sum(red, r, tt, waves=(0, 4)), row_sum(red, r, tt, waves=(1, 5))
+    )
+    uv = first.select(
+        row_sum(red, r, tt, waves=(2, 6)), row_sum(red, r, tt, waves=(3, 7))
+    )

+@traced
+def run_ug(c, nu):
+    """Every ug task of the step (|U| x 16) over the grid, reversed placement
+    (CTA b: tasks 255 - b, + 256, ...: the leftover tasks of the last round go
+    to the high CTAs, whose early work ends first), the next task's weights in
+    flight under this one's MFMAs; the last task issues none. A CTA with no
+    task (``nu == 0`` included) issues its first loads out of range."""
+    total = nu * UG_GROUPS
+    task = BLOCKS - 1 - fx.Int32(c["bid"])

+        task = nxt
+        ops = ops_n

+# ---------------------------------------------------------------- down

+def down_loads(c, rgd, nu, b0, width):
+    """The w2 tiles (4 steps) and scale codes of a wave's batch of slots b0,
+    b0 + 8, ... (``width``, ``down_width``; past |U| out of range: zeros):
+    flat, tiles then scale words (``_down_slot`` takes a word's code). Pooled
+    rows 16 rgd .. of each expert."""
+    lane = c["lane"]
+    a = c["args"]
+    r_w = rsrc(a["w2"], W2_BYTES)
+    r_s = rsrc(a["w2s"], W2S_BYTES)
+    es = [_expert_or_past(c, b0 + WAVES * j, nu) for j in range(width)]
+    av = [
+        fp4_tile_load(r_w, es[j] * W2_EXPERT_DWORDS, rgd, INTER, st, lane * 4)
+        for j in range(width)
+        for st in range(W2_STEPS)
+    ]
+    sa = [
+        fx.Int32(
+            bo.buffer_load(
+                r_s,
+                scale_index(

+                dtype=T.i32,

+        )

+        for st in range(W2_STEPS)
+    ]

+def _inter_spec(rt, route, a, idx, pick):
+    """(poll spec, live) of INTER pair ``idx`` of a WAVE-UNIFORM pick ``pick``
+    (``wave + 8 i``: a wave's 64 words are one pick's): a dead pick's pair has
+    no producer, so the spec names the pick's own ROUTE pair instead (produced
+    for every row; ``load_route`` saw it current), whose value the caller
+    drops. The id goes through ``uniform``, so the base select is scalar and
+    the buffer resource stays in SGPRs."""
+    ok = _live(uniform(_pick_id(rt, pick)))
+    at = Addr(a.region, a.space, fx.Int64(ok.select(a.value, route.value)))
+    rix = id_index(pick // TOPK, pick % TOPK)
+    return (at, ok.select(idx, rix), 1), ok

+
+def _isc_spec(rt, route, idx, pick):
+    """(poll spec, live) of ISC pair ``idx`` of pick ``pick``, which differs
+    across a wave (16 codes a pick): as ``_inter_spec``, but the dead / live
+    choice is made in the INDEX over one wave-uniform base, ``route`` (ISC

+    would make the buffer resource divergent, and the compiler then wraps every
+    load of the poll loop in a readfirstlane waterfall. The spec keeps the
+    region name ``isc``; a give-up record never names it (a batch's record
+    names its first spec, an INTER one)."""
+    ok = _live(_pick_id(rt, pick))
+    at = Addr("isc", route.space, route.value)
+    rix = id_index(pick // TOPK, pick % TOPK)
+    return (at, ok.select(idx + ISC_FROM_ROUTE, rix), 1), ok

+@traced
+def load_inter(c):
+    """The step's INTER words and ISC codes -> LDS ``interq`` / ``intsc``, live
+    picks only: a dead pick (pad row, garbage id) has no producer, so it gets
+    zero words and the unit code without a poll (its pair is replaced in the
+    poll batch by the pick's own ROUTE pair, which ``load_route`` already saw
+    current, so the batch stays one round trip). Also zeroes ``contrib``."""

+    inter, route = scr["inter"], scr["route"]

+    nw = s * TOPK * INTER_WORDS  # a multiple of THREADS
+    nc = s * TOPK * UG_GROUPS
+    specs, oks = [], []
+    for i in range_constexpr(nw // THREADS):
+        idx = tid32 + THREADS * i  # pick idx // 64 = wave + 8 i
+        pick = fx.Int32(wave) + (THREADS // INTER_WORDS) * i
+        sp, ok = _inter_spec(rt, route, inter, idx, pick)
+        specs.append(sp)
+        oks.append(ok)
+    for i in range_constexpr((nc + THREADS - 1) // THREADS):
+        idx = fx.min(tid32 + THREADS * i, nc - 1)
+        sp, ok = _isc_spec(rt, route, idx, idx // UG_GROUPS)
+        specs.append(sp)
+        oks.append(ok)

+    for i in range_constexpr(nw // THREADS):

+        idx = tid32 + THREADS * i

+            )

+@traced

+    lane = c["lane"]

+    tok = lane % 16 < c["S"]

+                d["interq"] + inter_read_word(pick, st, kb, 0),
+                result_type=fx.Vector.make_type(4, fx.Int32),

+        bw = fx.Vector.from_elements(

+        )

+        sb = picked.select(code, fx.Int32(UNIT_SCALE))

+        sa = (ops[nbs + j * W2_STEPS + st] >> ((2 * (st % 2) + rgd % 2) * 8)) & 0xFF

+            bw,
+            acc,
+            sa,
+            sb,
+            FP4,
+            FP4,
+            0,
+            0,

+
+@traced

+def run_down(c, rgd, nu):

+to 16 token rows in LDS, one ``mfma_f32_16x16x32_bf16`` per 32 K.

+64 contiguous bytes of its row a chunk (4 dwordx4 at q 32 + g 8 elements: lane

+inside a chunk is a permutation both operands share, so the dot is unchanged.

+ROWS = 16
+KCH = 128
+LDS_PAD = 8  # bf16 a padded token row
+
+
+def chunks(k):
+    """A wave's K chunks for K = ``k``: (count a wave, total)."""
+    n = k // KCH
+    return (n + WAVES - 1) // WAVES, n
+
+
+def loads(lane, wave, w, row0, k, nt=True, ldk=None, k0=0):
+    """This wave's operands of weight rows ``row0`` .. + 16 (row-major, ``ldk``
+    bf16 a row at ``w``, K columns ``k0`` .. ``k0 + k``): a list a chunk
+    (clamped into K: ``mfmas`` zeroes the extra)."""
+    per, n = chunks(k)
+    ldk = k if ldk is None else ldk
+    r_w = rsrc(w)
+    row = row0 + lane % ROWS
+    g = lane // ROWS
+    out = []
+    for i in range(per):
+        ch = fx.min(wave + WAVES * i, n - 1)
+        base = (row * ldk + k0 + ch * KCH + g * 8) // 2
+        out.append(
+            [
+                fx.Vector(
+                    bo.buffer_load(
+                        r_w,
+                        base + 16 * q,
+                        vec_width=4,
+                        dtype=T.i32,
+                        cache_modifier=CM_NT if nt else 0,
+                    )
+                )
+                for q in range(4)
+            ]
+        )
+    return out
+
+
+def mfmas(lane, wave, xl, xrow, k, s, ops):
+    """``loads``' operands against token rows 0 .. s - 1 of the LDS rows ``xl``
+    (``xrow`` bf16 a row) -> this wave's 16x16 accumulator."""
+    per, n = chunks(k)
+    g = lane // ROWS
+    t = fx.min(lane % ROWS, s - 1)
+    acc = fx.Vector.filled(4, 0.0, fx.Float32)
+    for i in range_constexpr(per):
+        ch = wave + WAVES * i
+        live = ch < n
+        kk = fx.min(ch, n - 1) * KCH + g * 8
+        for q in range_constexpr(4):
+            xb = fx.Vector(
+                fx.ptr_load(
+                    xl + (t * xrow + kk + 32 * q) // 2,
+                    result_type=fx.Vector.make_type(4, fx.Int32),
+                )
+            )
+            if const_live(per, n):
+                xb = fx.Vector.from_elements(
+                    [live.select(xb[d], fx.Int32(0)) for d in range(4)], fx.Int32
+                )
+            acc = mfma_bf16(
+                ops[i][q].bitcast(fx.BFloat16), xb.bitcast(fx.BFloat16), acc
+            )
+    return acc
+
+
+def const_live(per, n):
+    """Whether some wave's last chunk is past K (its MFMA must add zero)."""
+    return per * WAVES != n
+
+
+@traced
+def rows_to_lds(tid, src, k, s, xl, xrow, cm=0, ldk=None, k0=0):
+    """Columns k0 .. k0 + k of token rows 0 .. s - 1 of the bf16 [s, ldk] at
+    ``src`` -> LDS (``xrow`` a row), 16 B a lane."""
+    ldk = k if ldk is None else ldk
+    words = s * k // 8
+    for i in range_constexpr((words + THREADS - 1) // THREADS):
+        e = fx.min(tid + THREADS * i, words - 1)
+        t = e // (k // 8)
+        kk = e % (k // 8) * 8
+        v = fx.Vector(
+            bo.buffer_load(
+                rsrc(src),
+                (t * ldk + k0 + kk) // 2,
+                vec_width=4,
+                dtype=T.i32,
+                cache_modifier=cm,
+            )
+        )
+        if tid + THREADS * i < words:
+            fx.ptr_store(v, xl + (t * xrow + kk) // 2)
+    gpu.barrier()

+"""K2 phase 2c and 3a (README, "K2 program order"): the pooler and the
+pre-expert norm + MXFP4 a1.
+
+    pooler  (CTA P0 + task, task < 128: g = task // 4, q = task % 4) pooled
+            columns n0 = 512 rank + 16 g .. + 16 against ffn_in's K quarter q
+            (``xrow``, the 16 seam slices covering it): a 16-row bf16 GEMV
+            (``gemv``); parts q > 0 hand their fp32 partials to part 0
+            (PPART), which adds them in part order, rounds to bf16 once and
+            all-gathers the rows (every rank's POOL).
+    load_xq (every CTA that can get a ug task: ``spec.ug_cta0``) all 4096
+            pooled columns of every row -> the pre-expert RMSNorm
+            (``fused_rmsnorm_expand``: x rsqrt(mean x^2 + eps), times
+            (w + 1), bf16) -> MXFP4 a1 by aiter's HIP RoundUp rule
+            (``fused_dynamic_mx_quant_moe_sort``: a 32-group's amax floored at
+            1e-10, the ceil code of amax * f32(1/6), RNE e2m1) -> LDS ``xq``
+            (fp4 words) and ``xsc`` (codes), the ug stage's B operand.
+
+Every such CTA computes identical a1 bytes from identical inputs, so nothing is
+handed off. A pad row's normed values are zeros by ``select`` (its a1 is fp4
+zeros with the floor's code 92).
+
+The pooler is K3's early latent task (pr60683 ``mono/stages/moe.py``
+``early_loads`` / ``early_compute`` / ``early_out``) at Muse's shapes;
+``load_xq`` is K3's ``load_latq`` with the norm and the 1e-10 floor added.
+"""

+import functools
+
+import flydsl.expr as fx
+from aiter.ops.flydsl.kernels import buffer_ops as bo

+from flydsl.expr import math as fmath
+from flydsl.expr.typing import T
+
+from vllm.models.muse_spark.amd.specialized_decode.mono.common.mx import (
+    e8m0_roundup,
+    pk_fp4_bf16,
+    pow2,
+)
+from vllm.models.muse_spark.amd.specialized_decode.mono.common.ops import (
+    CM_DEV,
+    bf2_f32,
+    bf16_pair,
+    hw_rsq,
+    ld_pad,
+    row_sum,
+    rsrc,
+    traced,
+    wave_sum,
+)
+from vllm.models.muse_spark.amd.specialized_decode.mono.common.plan import (
+    cdiv,

+from vllm.models.muse_spark.amd.specialized_decode.mono.spec import (
+    AMAX_FLOOR,
+    COLS,
+    GAIN,
+    HIDDEN,
+    MOE_HIDDEN,
+    OWN_COLS,
+    P_K,
+    P_PARTS,
+    PRE_EXP_EPS,
+    ROWS,
+    THREADS,
+    TP,
+    XQ_WORDS,
+    XROW,
+    XSC_WORDS,
+    pool_pair,

+XL_ROW = P_K + gemv.LDS_PAD  # bf16 a token row of the pooler's LDS x slice
+SLICES_A_PART = P_K // COLS  # 16 seam slices cover a K quarter

+GROUP_WORDS = GROUP // 2  # 16 bf16 pair words a group
+assert XSC_WORDS * GROUP == MOE_HIDDEN and XQ_WORDS * 8 == MOE_HIDDEN

+
+@functools.cache
+def lds_struct(s: int):
+    """The pooler's LDS: the K quarter of rows 0 .. s-1 of ffn_in (bf16, a
+    row every ``XL_ROW``)."""
+
+    @fx.struct
+    class PoolLds:
+        xl: fx.Array[fx.Int32, s * XL_ROW // 2, 16]
+
+    return PoolLds
+
+
+@functools.cache
+def xq_lds_struct(s: int):
+    """``load_xq``'s LDS, live until the last ug task (K2's layer build
+    composes it with ``experts.ug_lds_struct`` as ``xq_ug``): ``xq`` row t's
+    fp4 words (word ``t 512 + 4 kb + w``: K ``32 kb + 8 w ..``), ``xsc`` its
+    e8m0 codes (a word each, ``t 128 + kb``), ``xss`` the 32-groups' sums of
+    squares."""
+
+    @fx.struct
+    class XqLds:
+        xq: fx.Array[fx.Int32, s * XQ_WORDS, 16]
+        xsc: fx.Array[fx.Int32, s * XSC_WORDS, 16]
+        xss: fx.Array[fx.Float32, s * XSC_WORDS, 16]
+
+    return XqLds
+
+
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------- pooler
+
+
+def _task(c, task):
+    """(g, q, n0): the pooler task's row group, K quarter and first pooled
+    column (row of ``w_pool``)."""
+    g = task // P_PARTS
+    q = task % P_PARTS
+    return g, q, c["rank"] * OWN_COLS + g * ROWS
+
+
+def pool_loads(c, task):
+    """Pooler task ``task``'s ``w_pool`` operands for this wave: rows n0 .. +16,
+    K ``2048 q ..`` (2 chunks a wave, nontemporal). Issued before the XRDY
+    waits."""
+    _, q, n0 = _task(c, task)
+    return gemv.loads(
+        c["lane"], c["wave"], c["args"]["w_pool"], n0, P_K, ldk=HIDDEN, k0=q * P_K
+    )
+
+
+@traced
+def stage_pool(c, task, ops):
+    """Pooler task ``task``: its K quarter of rows 0 .. S-1 of xrow -> LDS
+    (after the 16 seam slices covering it) -> ``gemv.mfmas`` -> fp32 rows.
+    q > 0: PPART. q == 0: + the 3 parts in part order -> bf16 -> every rank's
+    POOL (element ``t 4096 + col``)."""
+    s, tid, lane, wave, red = c["S"], c["tid"], c["lane"], c["wave"], c["red"]
+    g, q, n0 = _task(c, task)
+    xl = c["lds"]["pool"]["xl"]
+    if tid < SLICES_A_PART:
+        c["poll"]([(c["scr"]["xrdy"], q * SLICES_A_PART + tid, 1)])
+    gpu.barrier()

+        tid, c["scr"][XROW], P_K, s, xl, XL_ROW, CM_DEV, ldk=HIDDEN, k0=q * P_K
+    )
+    acc = gemv.mfmas(lane, wave, xl, XL_ROW, P_K, s, ops)
+    fx.ptr_store(acc, red + (wave * 64 + lane) * 4)
+    gpu.barrier()
+    if (q > 0) & (tid < s * ROWS):
+        r = tid % ROWS
+        t = tid // ROWS
+        c["put"](c["scr"]["ppart"], ppart_pair(g, q, t, r), row_sum(red, r, t))

+        rp = tid % (ROWS // 2)
+        t = tid // (ROWS // 2)
+        # rows 2 rp and 2 rp + 1 are adjacent pairs of each part
+        got = c["poll"](
+            [
+                (c["scr"]["ppart"], ppart_pair(g, qq, t, 2 * rp), 2)
+                for qq in range(1, P_PARTS)
+            ]
+        )
+        v0 = row_sum(red, 2 * rp, t)
+        v1 = row_sum(red, 2 * rp + 1, t)
+        for qq in range_constexpr(P_PARTS - 1):
+            v0 = v0 + got[qq][0].bitcast(fx.Float32)
+            v1 = v1 + got[qq][1].bitcast(fx.Float32)
+        at = t * MOE_HIDDEN + n0 + 2 * rp
+        for p in range_constexpr(TP):
+            c["put_bf"](c["peer"]["pool"][p], at, [v0, v1])
+    gpu.barrier()
+
+
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------- a1
+
+
+def _group_quant(ws, wq, r, pad_t):
+    """A 32-group: pooled bf16 pair words ``ws`` (16), pre-expert weight pair
+    words ``wq`` (16), the row's rsqrt ``r``, its pad flag -> (the e8m0 code,
+    the 4 fp4 words). xe = bf16((p r) (w + 1)), as
+    ``_rmsnorm_expand_kernel``; then the HIP RoundUp quant of those bf16."""
+    xe = []
+    am = fx.Int32(0)
+    for m in range(GROUP_WORDS):
+        p0, p1 = bf2_f32(ws[m])
+        w0, w1 = bf2_f32(wq[m])
+        y0 = (p0 * r) * (w0 + fx.Float32(GAIN))
+        y1 = (p1 * r) * (w1 + fx.Float32(GAIN))
+        word = bf16_pair(y0, y1).bitcast(fx.Int32)
+        word = fx.Int32(pad_t.select(fx.Int32(0), word))
+        xe.append(word)
+        # |bf16| ordered as its magnitude bits (finite values)
+        am = fx.max(am, word & 0x7FFF)
+        am = fx.max(am, (word >> 16) & 0x7FFF)

+    code = e8m0_roundup(amax)
+    scale = pow2(code)
+    pks = []
+    for w in range(GROUP // 8):
+        pk = fx.Int32(0)
+        for j in range(4):
+            pk = pk_fp4_bf16(pk, xe[4 * w + j], scale, j)
+        pks.append(pk)
+    return code, pks
+
+
+@traced
+def load_xq(c):
+    """POOL (all 4096 columns of rows 0 .. S-1) -> pre-expert norm -> MXFP4:
+    LDS ``xq`` / ``xsc`` (and ``tot``: a row's sum of squares). Thread a
+    32-group b = tid + 512 i: row t = b // 128, columns ``32 kb ..``
+    (kb = b % 128)."""
+    s, tid, lane, wave = c["S"], c["tid"], c["lane"], c["wave"]
+    a = c["args"]
+    lds = c["lds"]["xq"]
+    xq, xsc, xss = lds["xq"], lds["xsc"], lds["xss"]
+    tot = c["rt"]["tot"]
+    ngrp = s * XSC_WORDS
+    r_w = rsrc(a["w_preexp"])
+    # every round's weights and pad byte before the first POOL wait (the
+    # "loads before waits" rule: at S > 4 a thread has two rounds)
+    pre = []
+    for i in range_constexpr(cdiv(ngrp, THREADS)):
+        b = fx.min(tid + THREADS * i, ngrp - 1)
+        t = b // XSC_WORDS
+        kb = b % XSC_WORDS
+        wq = []
+        for h in range_constexpr(GROUP_WORDS // 4):
+            v = fx.Vector(
+                bo.buffer_load(r_w, kb * GROUP_WORDS + 4 * h, vec_width=4, dtype=T.i32)
+            )
+            wq += [v[e] for e in range(4)]
+        pre.append((i, b, t, kb, wq, ld_pad(a["pad"], t)))
+    groups = []
+    for i, b, t, kb, wq, pad_t in pre:
+        got = c["poll"](
+            [
+                (c["peer"]["pool_own"], pool_pair(t, GROUP * kb) + 2 * jj, 2)
+                for jj in range(GROUP_WORDS // 2)
+            ]
+        )
+        ws = [got[jj][m] for jj in range(GROUP_WORDS // 2) for m in range(2)]
+        gss = fx.Float32(0.0)
+        for m in range_constexpr(GROUP_WORDS):
+            p0, p1 = bf2_f32(ws[m])
+            gss = fx.Float32(fmath.fma(p0, p0, gss))
+            gss = fx.Float32(fmath.fma(p1, p1, gss))

+    if wave < s:

+            xss + (wave * XSC_WORDS + 64 + lane)

+        if tid + THREADS * i < ngrp:
+            for w in range_constexpr(GROUP // 8):
+                fx.ptr_store(pks[w], xq + (t * XQ_WORDS + kb * (GROUP // 8) + w))
+            fx.ptr_store(code, xsc + (t * XSC_WORDS + kb))
+    gpu.barrier()
